name: Impossibilism
summary: Impossibilism is the Marxist position that capitalism cannot be reformed into socialism and that a working-class party should campaign only for common ownership and democratic control of production, not for a programme of reforms. Its adherents hold that a conscious majority must win political power peacefully and democratically, reject vanguard parties, nationalisation as socialism and Bolshevik state capitalism, and look to a world without money, wages or states.
scope: The anti-reformist Marxist tradition of the Socialist Party of Great Britain, the World Socialist Movement companion parties and the Socialist Party of Canada, in their mature form. De Leonism and its industrial-union strategy have their own entry and are left out; early Canadian inconsistencies (reform demands, anti-Asian views) are treated as superseded by the mature position.
